title: Steward scrub & signal catalog — lightweight telemetry for cross-functional canaries
body:
Purpose:
This note collects a compact signal catalog and a lightweight stewarding checklist we can use for small-batch canaries and A/B experiments across Console-managed routes. Goal is a repeatable, low-friction ritual that: 
- surfaces cross-functional ownership (product, SRE, runtime, privacy),
- codifies simple pass/fail heuristics for ramp decisions, and
- provides short synthetic args to reduce noisy human coordination during an activation window.

Context / constraints (working assumptions):
- Target experiments: model swaps, prompt/template changes, reranker adjustments, token budget knobs.
- Typical ramp: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% (we allow custom paths for high-sensitivity features).
- Timebox per step: 30–90m for quick safety checks; 24–48h for quality/metrics-driven ramps.
- We prefer conservative auto-shelving (auto-disable) only for clear infrastructure/latency/availability failures; quality regressions should trigger human review unless we have validated automatic signal proxies.

Signal families (what to monitor):
1) Availability & infra signals (SRE primary)
   - 5xx rate (route-level) — one-minute and five-minute. Alert if > baseline + 0.5 percentage points AND absolute > 0.2%
   - p95/p99 latency (inference tail) — compare to baseline cohort (same route + model family). Alert if p95 > baseline * 1.5 for two consecutive windows
   - GPU throttles / OOMs / cold-starts — telemetry + logs. Any OOM triggers immediate rollback.
2) Cost / tokens (eng/runtime + product)
   - average tokens per request — if > baseline * 1.4 for sustained 1h, flag for cost review
   - token spend rate per minute (rollup) to detect runaway prompts or loops
3) Functional correctness & quality proxies (product + ML)
   - Regression eval set score (periodic background eval using lighthouse prompts) — primary quality gate for progressive ramps
   - Production proxy: embedding-drift vs historical (mean cosine drop) for user content — large drift may indicate hallucination or template mismatch
   - Duplicate-reply / truncated-response rate — heuristics to catch truncation regressions after context or token limit changes
4) Safety / content (policy + security)
   - Safety classifier trigger rate — compare to baseline; sudden increase may require throttling
   - PII / sensitive-identifiers detection heuristics triggered (privacy owner)
5) User-visible business metrics (GTM / product)
   - conversion funnel delta for traffic slices (if available) — small-sample uplift should be treated carefully (high variance)
   - user satisfaction proxies (thumbs up/down, retention events) — flagged for post-rollout analysis

Instrumentation & lightweight dashboards:
- Minimum required: route-level time series for 5xx, p95/p99, avg tokens/request, token spend/min, safety-triggers/min.
- Add a single combined "Canary Health" score (0–100) computed from weighted z-scores of the above signals (see appendix toy weights). Use it for quick human scanning, not sole decisionmaker.
- Tag all canary traffic with experiment_id and steward_id so we can filter logs/traces without mixing cohorts.

Steward roles (minimum viable):
- Experiment owner (product/feature PM) — hypothesis, success criteria, primary comms
- Steward (rotating) — runs the pre-launch checklist, monitors dashboards during ramp windows, executes rollback if criteria hit, writes quick timeline notes
- Runtime lead (eng-serving-runtime) — ensures model variant compatibility and capacity; pre-validates quantization/latency assumptions
- SRE on-call liaison — monitors infra signals and authorizes auto-shelving for infra failures
- Privacy / Legal reviewer (as needed) — signs off for datasets or prompt templates with potential PII handling

Pre-launch checklist (quick):
- [ ] Define primary metric(s) + pass/fail thresholds (exact numbers in experiment ticket)
- [ ] Link evaluation snapshot and baseline cohort (eval script + dataset id)
- [ ] Confirm instrumentation tags and dashboard panels (experiment_id present)
- [ ] Synthetic canary run (see recipe below) + smoke-test responses for expected tone/length
- [ ] Token limits and cost guardrails set (per-route budget + soft throttle)
- [ ] Rollback owner and communication channel set (Slack + incident channel)

Synthetic canary recipe (cheap, privacy-safe):
- Create a 50–200 sample synthetic suite derived from anonymized real prompts + adversarial edge cases. Run locally and on-hosted variant at scale 10x to check throughput and tail latency.
- Expected outputs: short-checklist: length distribution, typical token delta vs baseline, example golden responses for 10 seed prompts.

Launch day run ritual (for short ramps):
- T0: open experiment ticket and attach steward checklist. Confirm channels (Slack thread pinned).
- After deployment to 0.1%: steward observes 30m windows for infra/cost signals, runs quick spot-check of 10 user responses.
- If no signals -> ramp to 1% and repeat (45–90m).
- At 5%/25% wait longer (2–24h) and prioritize running batch evals on collected traffic if feasible.

Escalation matrix (condensed):
- Infra critical (OOM/large % 5xx/persistent p99 blowouts): SRE triggers auto-shelve + rollback. Immediate: steward posts incident stub and alerts SRE pager.
- Cost runaway (tokens/min > 3x baseline): runtime lead can throttle route; steward notifies finance/PM.
- Quality regression (eval score drop > threshold or embedding drift > threshold): steward pauses ramp and requests Product/ML deep-dive; manual rollback if egregious.
- Safety spike: privacy/legal triage; default: reduce exposure to 0 while investigating.

Rollback taxonomy (quick):
- Auto-rollback: infra availability failures, OOMs, critical security signals.
- Manual-rollback (fast): quality regressions flagged by steward + product.
- Slow-rollback (deprioritized): subtle long-term quality drift requiring model-retraining or prompt redesign.

Pass/fail heuristics (toy examples — to put in ticket):
- Fail: 5xx rate > baseline + 0.5pp AND absolute 5xx > 0.2% within 10m -> auto-shelve
- Fail: p95 latency > baseline*1.5 for two consecutive 5m windows -> auto-shelve (if also causes request timeouts)
- Review: embedding mean cosine drop > 0.07 over 1h -> steward review (manual hold)
- Review: Eval-set score drop > 3% absolute -> hold and triage

Post-launch quick retro template (to fill within 72h):
- Window summary: times, slices, percent exposures, steward(s) on duty
- Signals observed (bullet): infra, latency, cost, safety, quality
- Actions taken: rollback, throttles, notebook/PR links
- Root cause hypothesis (short) + next step owners
- Data retention note: keep canary logs flagged for 30d (default)

Open questions / TODOs (explicit):
- How do we bake privacy-preserving golden comparisons into Console so PMs can run evals without infra ops? (Design ticket?)
- Experiment health score weights need calibration; propose a small A/B of the score itself across past canaries to tune weights
- Should we allow auto-rollbacks for certain quality proxies (embedding drift) if we've validated that proxy against eval set? (risk appetite discussion)

Appendix: toy weights for Canary Health score (example, subject to calibration):
- Infra 40% (5xx + p99), latency 20%, cost 10%, quality proxies 20%, safety 10%

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep this doc intentionally concise — main productization will live in a confluence page + ticket template.
- Candidate next step: small runtime feature to auto-annotate canary logs with steward_id and experiment_id at route ingress.

References & quick links: added to linked_artifacts above.

(End of draft — this is a working doc. Comments appreciated. — Aisha)
